bias: Financial conditions are re-tightening at the long end and in credit, while the front end and equities have not followed. Since Monday Sep 28 the 30Y has climbed 10bp to 5.633% (13bp above the 5.5% stress line) and the 10Y 6bp to 5.281%, even as the 2Y rallied 9bp to 4.827% -- a bear steepening that widens 2s10s to 45bp from 30bp. Real yields hit fresh cycle highs (DFII5 2.73%, DFII10 2.93%) against flat breakevens (2.36%), so this remains a term-premium/real-rate story, not an inflation scare, with oil (-3.5%) pulling the other way. What changed versus the last run is confirmation: MOVE jumped to 107.6 (from 96.0) and HY OAS widened to 3.24% (from ~2.8%, now close to the 3.5% line), with CACC -5.4% and HYG -1.2%. Offsetting this, the Asia selloff of Sep 28 has fully reversed -- the Korea gate reopens 3/3 -- VIX is lower at 15.57, SOFR-IORB is -3bp and the quarter-end passed without a funding spike. Net: duration and credit stress is building at the margin but equity vol, funding and the Korea/Asia complex are not yet corroborating. Watch the 9:30am ET open, today's H.8 print, and the Oct 6-8 3Y/10Y/30Y auctions -- a weak long-end auction into a 30Y above 5.6% would be the clearest test.

counterargs.read: The evidence is split by channel rather than by time. Duration and credit are now corroborating each other -- the 30Y is 13bp over the stress line, MOVE has jumped 12% and HY OAS is within ~26bp of the 3.5% threshold -- which is the Group A + B/C pattern the framework treats as a risk-off transition signal. But the channels that usually accompany a genuine liquidity shock (VIX, funding, Asian equities, semis) are all benign or improving, and breakevens/oil say it is not inflation. The consistent reading is a term-premium/supply-driven long-end selloff that is starting to leak into credit, not yet a broad liquidity contraction. The Oct 6-8 auction cluster and any further HY widening past 3.5% are the tests that would upgrade or fade it.

treasury_auctions.narrative: Oct 2 update: no new auctions since the Sep 24 7Y; the Sep 22-24 Note trio and the Sep 17 TIPS reopening settled Sep 30. The three-straight thin-indirect pattern (2Y 49.3%, 5Y 47.0%, 7Y 49.1%) remains the unresolved question, and the module holds at EARLY WARNING with absorption 47 / dealer stress 49 unchanged. This is still duration repricing rather than confirmed Treasury intermediation stress: dealer take-down is not rising, repo is normal (SOFR-IORB -3bp) and quarter-end passed without a funding spike -- but the long end has since sold off further (US30Y 5.633%, +10bp) and MOVE has jumped to 107.6, so the upcoming 3Y (Oct 6), 10Y reopening (Oct 7) and 30Y reopening (Oct 8) are a genuine test of whether end-investor demand returns at higher yields. Prior detail: The 7Y (91282CRM5, Sep 24) settled decently on the metrics that matter most for dealer stress: BTC 2.42 and dealer take-down 10.76%, both roughly in line with the two comparable 7Y prints in the ledger (Aug 27: BTC 2.50/dealer 10.84%; Jul 28: BTC 2.49/dealer 11.7%). But indirect demand was again soft at 49.13% -- below both those comps (53.72%, 63.0%) and in the same range as the Sep 22 2Y (49.27%) and Sep 23 5Y (46.98%). That makes three straight Note auctions with thinning indirect (often foreign/end-investor) demand, even though only the 5Y also showed elevated dealer take-down. The module holds at EARLY WARNING: this is not a third weak print on every metric (no escalation to Intermediation Stress), but it is not a clean auction either (no downgrade to Healthy). Separately from the auction story, US10Y and US30Y kept selling off into today's session (+11.1bp/+11.7bp since the prior run), with the 30Y crossing the 5.5% long-end stress line for the first time and MOVE spiking a further +9.6% to 104.58. Funding remains normal (SOFR-IORB -2bp, repo_confirmation false) and credit is calm, so this stays short of Intermediation Stress. The next test is the H.8 bank-demand read today a

transmission.bottom_line: The long-end selloff has resumed and, unlike the prior run, bond vol and credit now confirm it.
